output.brief: The August dip was almost entirely caused by the failure of the east-riser chiller (CH-2), which left floors 6-8 at 26-29 C from 4 to 19 August. Those floors' room-comfort score fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4, and it was back to 8.4 once cooling was restored. Floors 1-5 barely moved. Of the negative comments, 56 were about heat, all from floors 6-8. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates (95%), kiosk queue times and check-in scores were all unchanged. So I would not serve notice on Orrin or pull the kiosks. The survey questionnaire and invitation method did not change. The 6% rate rise may have nudged value-for-money down a little on floors 1-5, but that dip is similar to the usual August seasonal dip and I can't separate the two. I would not reverse the rate rise yet, and I would not drop the August responses from the reported score. Next steps: reinstate the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spare parts on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. A further return-stay offer to affected guests is optional, since they already received an apology and half a night's credit. I'm fairly confident, about 85%. The main open question is the rate effect, which you could track through the weekly rate reviews.
